full_judgment:
4. Mr. Jaman Akter the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner disclosing the chain of title of the petitioners submits that the property in question is in possession of the petitioners and the property was included in the "kha" schedule of the gazette as vested property on 12-8-2012 and subsequently government has left all sorts of title and interest over the '`kha" schedule property by inserting section 28ka in the “অর্পিত সম্পত্তি আইন-২০০১ vide second amendment of the Act -2001 in the year 2013 (Act 46 of 2013). Learned Advocate further submits that Ministry of Land vide circular issued under memo No. 31.00.0000.045.53. 065.12 (part)-242 dated 22-5-2014 gave some sorts of instructions in respect of mutation, opening new holdings and receiving land revenues of "kha" schedule properties under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the "kha" schedule properties will be treated as khash land if it is not claimed and mutated by the respective claimants within I (one) year from the date of aforementioned circular. Learned Advocate contended that the respondents ought to mutate the name of the petitioners as per circular dated 22-5-2014 and receive the land revenue from the petitioners but the respondent No. 6 and 4 defying the said circular are trying to include the property in question in the "ka" schedule of the gazette violating the provisions of law. Learned Advocate finally submits that the apprehension of the petitioners regard to inclusion of the property in question in the "ka" schedule of the gazette becomes true while the respondent No. 4 Deputy Commissioner, Kushtia in the affidavit-in-opposition clearly admitted that it is under process to include the property in the "ka" schedule of the gazette of the vested properties, as such, a direction is required upon the respondents not to include the property in question in the ka schedule gazette of the vested properties. 

 9. The grievance of the petitioners is that though Government left the right, title and interest over the "kha" schedule property by inserting section 28ka in the Act-2001 and the property of the petitioners admittedly being -kha" scheduled property, the respondent No. 6 Assistant Commissioner land and respondent No.4 Deputy Commissioner, kushtia are not mutating the name of the petitioners defying the aforementioned circular dated 22-5-2014, rather, in violation of the provisions of law trying to include the property in question in the -ka" schedule gazette of the vested properties. This apprehension of the petitioners seems true while the respondent No. 4. Deputy Commissioner, Kushtia in the affidavit -in- opposition admitted that the land in question is under process to be included in the -ka" schedule of the gazette of the vested properties. This Court got no satisfactory answer from the learned DAG on the query of the court that if the property is leased out to kumarkhali Degree College under VP. Lease Case No. 02 (X)/1991 how it was included in the "kha" schedule of the gazette and further learned DAG failed to show us any provision of law that empowered the respondents to start process to include the property in question in the "ka" schedule of the gazette while government completed publication of final gazette notification of vested properties under section 9 of “অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন-২০০১ (সংশোধিত-২০১১)” We also found nothing in the Act- 2001 that empowered the authority to publish further gazette of -ka" schedule including more properties in the schedule. However, the government can seek remedy through usual course of law under sub section 4 of section 28ka of the Act-2001 if any government interest is involved with any "kha" schedule properties even after cancellation of kha schedule gazette. There is no scope in the law to include any more property in the "ka" schedule by publishing further gazette. Now-a-days it is a very common allegation that the Assistant Commissioners (land) are very reluctant to receive and dispose of the mutation application of the parties filed under section 143 of the State Acquision and Tenancy Act and further they are keeping pending mutation applications for uncertain period. The Assistant commissions (land) are assigned by the Government in the land revenue offices to render services to the public in accordance with law. They should not create unnecessary hassle or harass the people at large. The respondents should not act arbitrarily but to proceed in accordance with law while dealing with a mutation proceeding. We find that the petitioners have filed an application under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 to the respondent No. 6, Assistant Commissioner land, Kumarkhali which was received by his office on 14-11-2014 (Annexure 'D' to the writ petition) for mutation but the said application was not disposed of nor any mutation case number was given to start mutation proceeding. It is the statutory duty of the concern officer to dispose of the application under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 read with rule 23 of the State Acquisition Rule, 1955. We have already discussed above the legal proposition of law in dealing with the "kha" schedule properties. In the premises discussed above we think it will be fit and proper to direct the respondent No.6 to dispose of the application for mutation already received by the office of the respondent 6 on 14-11-2014 (Annexure-D) in accordance with law.
